title: Korean Dangi Calendar
intro: Traditional Korean lunisolar reckoning combines lunar months and the seasonal solar year. Dangi year numbering is associated with Korea's legendary founder Dangun.

steps.heading: Start with the lunar month
steps.text: Months begin around the new moon and usually contain 29 or 30 days.

steps.heading: Allow for a leap month
steps.text: Certain years include an additional whole lunar month, rather than the single extra day of the Gregorian leap year.

steps.heading: Distinguish year systems
steps.text: The Dangi era counts years differently from the Gregorian civil era; the month/day chronology must also be specified.

example: A traditional autumn lunar celebration can fall on different Gregorian dates in September or October. Identify the lunar year, month, day and leap-month status before conversion.
history: Korean lunisolar reckoning has long governed traditional festivals and seasonal life. The legendary foundation era is a chronological convention, not a modern astronomical measurement.
model: The provider owns Korean year tables for 1900–2100. Published KASI-based dates from 1900-01-31 through 2050-11-18 were checked independently; subsequent table dates are predictions. ICU supplies locale text and projection outside that range. Month navigation counts intercalary months separately. Year navigation from a leap month absent in the destination year selects the following ordinary month; day numbers clamp to the target month length. Zero-step navigation preserves the date.
limits: The model does not certify every historic court, locality or era. Future projections may differ from official calendars. South Korea's contemporary civil calendar is Gregorian. The date-only representation does not implement a sunset rollover.
sources: Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute: https://astro.kasi.re.kr/kor/life/pageView/5
